items.title: Lionel Hampton interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: So finally my wife, my late wife, Gladys, had got a guy

ctx.x: I tell you, I was always lucky. Because I was always seeking the fine youngsters, you know. They want to be musicians, and was waiting for a break to play in a big band. Because big bands was very popular then, just like when I left Benny Goodman and went out to get my band, there was little kids walking around in California, where I was staying at, after I left Benny Goodman, he took sick. And the doctors who were at the place warned him not to play no more for six months, because he had a disease called…

the clarinet. Well I told him I said “I want you to play tenor.” So finally my wife, my late wife, Gladys, had got a guy and went down to the [sounds like] Lucky Music Company. That’s where all the musicians traded with, and gave him a tenor saxophone, and then we had Marshall Royal, who was a great saxophone player. Marshall, when his brother was coming up, Ernie Royal, Ernie Royal could play really high notes on trumpet.
Did you put him on lead then?
